title: How to Find Construction Jobs in the UK Without an Agency
description: A practical guide for UK tradespeople on finding site work directly through platforms like SiteCrew — no recruiter fees, faster applications, and verified employers.

sections.heading: Why skip the agency?
paragraphs: Agencies can add delays and fees between you and the company hiring on site. Direct platforms let you see the role, rate, and location upfront — then apply in minutes.
SiteCrew connects verified construction companies with skilled workers across the UK. You browse open jobs, set your trades, and message employers directly.

sections.heading: Steps to get started
paragraphs: Create a free worker profile and add your main trade interests.
Browse jobs by trade or city — for example electrician roles in London or dryliner jobs in Manchester.
Apply to roles that match your availability and day rate expectations.

sections.heading: Browse jobs on SiteCrew
paragraphs: Start on the jobs page to see live openings, or explore trade-specific pages like electrician jobs or city pages such as construction jobs in Birmingham.

title: UK Construction Day Rates: What Tradespeople Should Know in 2026
description: Understand how day rates work on UK construction sites, what affects pay by trade, and how to compare open roles on SiteCrew.

sections.heading: How day rates are set
paragraphs: Day rates vary by trade, location, project type, and urgency. Electricians, dryliners, bricklayers, and labourers often negotiate rates per shift rather than annual salary.
Companies posting on SiteCrew list rates on each job so you can compare before applying.

sections.heading: Location matters
paragraphs: London and the South East typically command higher rates than regional cities, but cost of living and travel should factor into your decision.
Use city job pages — Leeds, Manchester, Bristol, and others — to see what is live in your area.
